nodes.label: Contravariance (in T)
nodes.rationale: Safe when T is only accepted (consumers): anything that handles any Dancer can handle a SalsaDancer.

nodes.label: Covariance (out T)
nodes.rationale: Safe when T is only returned (producers); take IEnumerable<T>/IReadOnlyList<T> parameters rather than List<T>.

nodes.label: Open/Closed principle violation in TemplateParser
nodes.rationale: One dictionary and one Register overload per type means adding a new type edits the class in three places.

nodes.label: Strategy pattern (behaviour passed as parameter)
nodes.rationale: Calculator does not know which operation it runs; the caller decides by passing a delegate.

nodes.label: Type-keyed registry refactor of TemplateParser
nodes.rationale: A single Dictionary<Type, List<(Token, Resolve)>> makes T meaningful, requires no parser changes for new types and lets each object only examine its own registrations.

nodes.label: Generic repository with in/out split (V6, CQRS-style)
nodes.norm_label: generic repository with in/out split (v6, cqrs-style)
nodes.rationale: Splitting read (out) and write (in) interfaces is what makes the read side covariant; a salsa repository cannot be an IWriteRepository<Dancer> (CS0266).

nodes.label: IValidator<in T> / NameRequiredValidator

nodes.label: Read/Write Repository Split (IReadOnlyRepository<out T> / IWriteRepository<in T>)
nodes.norm_label: read/write repository split (ireadonlyrepository<out t> / iwriterepository<in t>)
nodes.rationale: Splitting read (out) and write (in) sides allows SalsaRepository as IReadOnlyRepository<Dancer> and AuditLogRepository as IWriteRepository<SalsaDancer>, while SalsaRepository as IWriteRepository<Dancer> is rejected (CS0266).

nodes.label: C# Interview Cheat Code
nodes.rationale: Refresher with rules, snippets and diagrams needed to answer every question in the fake technical interview; each section names the questions it solves.

nodes.label: Fake Technical Interview (C# OOP, Generics & Delegates)
nodes.norm_label: fake technical interview (c# oop, generics & delegates)
nodes.rationale: 48-question multiple-choice mock interview built only from what the repo demonstrates; each answer links to README section and proving code line.

nodes.label: Interview Answer Key & Scoring
nodes.rationale: Score bands: 40-48 interview-ready, 30-39 review advanced exercises, below 30 follow the learning path in README.

nodes.label: Interview Q9-Q15: override vs new (Method Hiding)
nodes.norm_label: interview q9-q15: override vs new (method hiding)

nodes.label: Abstract Class vs Interface
nodes.rationale: Abstract class: single inheritance, shared base with state/constructors; interface: many per class, capability contract with no instance fields.

nodes.label: Constructor Order (static -> base -> derived)
nodes.rationale: Static ctor once, then base ctor (implicit parameterless if no : base(...)), then derived body; : base(args) selects the base constructor.

nodes.label: Contravariance (in T, consumer)
nodes.rationale: Things go in to consumers: I<Base> converts to I<Child>; in T may only be accepted.

nodes.label: Covariance (out T, producer)
nodes.rationale: Things come out of producers: I<Child> converts to I<Base>; out T may only be returned (CS1961 otherwise).

nodes.label: Delegate as Strategy (Calculator.Math)
nodes.rationale: A delegate is a type-safe method reference letting the caller decide behaviour.

nodes.label: Invariance (List<T>)
nodes.rationale: List<T> reads and writes T, so neither direction is safe (CS0029).

nodes.label: 3-Step Method Lookup (Virtual Dispatch)
nodes.rationale: Find method on declared type; if not virtual run it; else run most-derived override on runtime type, skipping new methods.

nodes.label: Method Shadowing with new
nodes.rationale: Use new only when the base method cannot be made virtual (e.g. third-party code); if you own the base, prefer virtual/override. Casting to the parent runs the parent's method.

nodes.label: override -> Runtime Type Wins; new -> Declared Type Wins
nodes.norm_label: override -> runtime type wins; new -> declared type wins

nodes.label: Runtime Polymorphism & Implicit Upcasting
nodes.rationale: Upcasting child->base is implicit and safe; downcasting needs a cast and can fail.

nodes.label: readonly vs init vs private set
nodes.norm_label: readonly vs init vs private set
nodes.rationale: readonly: set only in initializer/constructor; init: only during object creation; private set: class can set any time. Trap: Player(int) never sets ID so it is Guid.Empty.

nodes.label: Generic Swap<T> with ref & Type Inference
nodes.norm_label: generic swap<t> with ref & type inference

nodes.label: TemplateParser Open/Closed Fix (Dictionary<Type, resolvers>)
nodes.rationale: One dictionary and one overload per type breaks Open/Closed; a single registry keyed by typeof(T) with Register<T>(string, Func<T,string?>) makes T meaningful.

nodes.label: TemplateParser Overload Resolution Traps (CS0121)
nodes.rationale: T is never used; the lambda body selects the overload; x => x.ToString() fits both and is ambiguous.

nodes.label: Variance Restrictions (reference types; interfaces & delegates only)
nodes.norm_label: variance restrictions (reference types; interfaces & delegates only)
nodes.rationale: Value types are not variant (CS0266, use .Cast<object>()); classes cannot declare variant type parameters (CS1960).
